answer: HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded): In the PCA on the forms of capital (12 Z-scored capitals, one observation per 100-yr slice), PC1 at the start of the Younger Bronze Age — 1100 BCE — is a pronounced LOCAL PEAK, markedly HIGHER than every subsequent 1000–500 BCE horizon. PC1(1100) ≈ +4.51, versus a subsequent-six mean of ≈ +1.43 (range +0.79 to +2.18); 1100 BCE is ~3.07 PC1 units above the subsequent mean and ~2.33 units above even the highest subsequent slice (1000 BCE, +2.18). The six later slices are lower and tightly compressed, with a mild downward drift toward 500 BCE. PC1 is a composite "capital-abundance" axis (top loadings: copper/gold ZCU_AU +0.41, pottery decoration Zkeverz +0.38, depots ZHort +0.34, hatchet/sword ZAxtSchwert +0.30, daggers ZDolch +0.27; negative: pottery form ZKeform −0.35, axes ZBeil −0.24). Interpretation: 1100 BCE marks a peak of overall capital accumulation at the onset of the YBA, followed by a step-down to lower, more stable capital levels through 500 BCE. This is robust: a window-only PCA (dropping the two zero-variance capitals ZSichel and ZKeform) yields the SAME qualitative picture, with 1100 BCE an even more isolated peak (+5.78) above an all-negative 1000–500 cluster.

payload.workflow: Parsed capital.csv with decimal-comma handling (verified negative signs). Built a 39-slice x 12-capital matrix from all Z-columns. Standardised each column (correlation-matrix PCA) and ran full-series PCA via numpy eigendecomposition (sklearn unavailable; equivalent up to sign), anchoring PC1 sign so the largest |loading| (ZCU_AU) is positive. Extracted PC1 scores per slice, compared 1100 BCE against the 1000-500 BCE group (mean/range/difference), inspected PC1 loadings, and ran a window-only sensitivity PCA dropping the two zero-variance capitals (ZSichel, ZKeform).
